Guides / 04—08

Understand dimensional weight without guessing rates

Carrier divisors vary by service and agreement; supply the applicable value yourself.

Vijeron · Updated 10 October 2026

Basic formula

Dimensional weight in kilograms equals external volume in cm³ divided by a divisor in cm³/kg. Take the divisor from the correct service terms and date. This site chooses no default.

Compare actual weight

Weigh the complete parcel in kilograms. Comparing actual and dimensional weight highlights a figure that may matter for billing, but carriers can apply different rounding, limits and exceptions.

Verify before purchase

Check the carrier's own calculator or tariff for the destination and service. Vijeron explains arithmetic, not prices or a guaranteed billable weight.

Worked example

A 13,824 cm³ parcel with an example divisor of 5,000 cm³/kg gives 2.7648 kg. The divisor is an example input, not a universal rule.

Watch out

Do not round or choose a divisor without checking the relevant carrier's terms.
